cases.name: Marcquius Clarrissa "Wendy" Timmons-Moore
cases.about: Her given name was pronounced "Mar-queese." She went by "Wendy" and was a fraternal twin with her sister Quinetta, with whom she was very close. In a telephone conversation I had with her sister Quinetta in November 2022, she said Wendy was hilarious, had a ridiculous sense of humor, loved reading romance novels, and owned many books. She was enlisted in the U.S. Army for 12 years and was an electrical engineer. Quinetta said their brother had passed a month before Wendy was murdered.
cases.narrative:
"Police went to check on Timmons-Moore after her co-workers reported that she hadn't been to work for two weeks, the autopsy report states.

Her partially decomposed body was found naked and restrained to her bed with multiple black plastic garbage bags cinched around her neck and held in place by an electrical cord and a zip-tie, according to the report. Duct tape also was wrapped in two directions around her face.

Her wrists were handcuffed and then zip-tied to her knees, and electrical cords bound the handcuffs to her ankles, which also were zip-tied and duct-taped together, according to the report."

cases.name: Tanajwa McMurray
cases.about:
Her Go Fund Me said, "She is a former correctional sergeant with Maury Correctional Institution and ended her career with the Department of Public Safety at Eastern Correctional Center."

She was a 911 dispatcher for Harnett and Cumberland counties. "She would always sacrifice a lot of things for her siblings [and] sacrifice a lot of stuff for her family," said her mother, Tasha McMurray. Tasha McMurray said her daughter had moved to Fayetteville to take care of her, and that, when she was killed, more than one life was taken from the family. Tanajwa McMurray was smart, caring and loving, according to her mother. "Tanjwa was my everything. It was nothing I could ask her that she would not do," she said. "She gave me smiles; she gave me joy."

cases.name: Barbara Mitchell Adair
cases.about:
Her obituary said, "Hello there, it's me, Barbara Adair, or as many of you affectionately, know me as Barb. Speaking to you one last time from beyond, I've always believe in the words of Emily Dickinson, " because I could not stop for death, he kindly stopped for me." and so, he has, and I've embarked on a journey to a place where the canvas of life is painted with eternal colors.
I was born on a chilly winter morning, on December 3, 1963, in Cumberland County, North Carolina. Today, I want to share my journey with you, not with a heavy heart, but with a smile, because we all know I was as lively as they come. I quickly discovered my love for the arts, particularly painting and sand art. I found joy in the simplicity of a brush stroke, the merging of colors, and the beauty that sprang forth from raw, untouched canvas. But my true masterpiece was not one that hung on the wall. It was, and forever will be, the family I so lovingly, stitch together with threads of compassion, loyalty, and unwavering love. Now, as I pass the baton to you, remember me, not with tears, but with smiles and laughter. Remember me in the sunrise, in the hues of a sunset, in the stroke of a paintbrush, and in the beauty of sand art. To quote the great Maya, Angelou, “I hope I made you feel loved, cherished, and valued, because that’s how you made me feel."

cases.name: Amanda Lynn Smith
cases.about:
Her obituary, "In her brief yet impactful life, Amanda’s vibrant personality shone through her diverse interests and passions, leaving an indelible mark on the hearts of those who knew her.

Amanda was known for her culinary skills, often bringing joy to family and friends with her delicious dishes. She found serenity in nature, spending many days fishing, where she felt connected to the beauty around her. A true creative, Amanda expressed herself through art and had a remarkable skill in 3D printing, showcasing her innovative spirit.

Her love for automobiles, particularly her fondness for Miata's, led her to partake in gatherings like the Miata's at the Gap at Tale of the Dragon, where enthusiasts convened to celebrate their shared passion. Amanda's enthusiasm for life was also mirrored in her affection for her beloved fur babies—Scrappy, Chaos, and Sammy—who were a significant part of her daily joy.

In life, Amanda shared a close bond with her fiancé, Perry Emanuel Turpin, who was a steadfast partner by her side for 12 years."
